column2: Which author wrote about rural society in Far from the Madding Crowd?
Also Jude the Obscure.
Who wrote Lucky Jim?
William Golding
He wrote more than {#} novels.
Which TWO novels did Graham Greene write?
Scoop
Our Man in Havana
Also The Heart of the Matter and The Honorary Consul.
Brighton Rock and Our Man in Havana
Which Anglo-Saxon poem tells of a hero’s battles against monsters?
Sir Gawain and the Green Knight
The Canterbury Tales
Paradise Lost
It is still translated into modern English.
Who wrote Paradise Lost?
Shakespeare
Inspired by his religious views.
Shakespeare wrote many sonnets.
From The Daffodils. Wordsworth was inspired by nature.
Who wrote "Tyger! Tyger! burning bright"?
John Keats
From The Tyger.
Which poem begins "Oh to be in England now that April’s there"?
Home Thoughts from Abroad, by Robert Browning
The Daffodils, by Wordsworth
If, by Kipling
The Tyger, by Blake
Robert Browning ({#}–{#}).
Which TWO poets wrote about their experiences in the First World War?
John Betjeman
Siegfried Sassoon
Ted Hughes
Owen wrote Anthem for Doomed Youth.
Wilfred Owen and Siegfried Sassoon
Sir Walter Scott’s poems were inspired by which area?
Scotland and the Borders
He also wrote novels, many set in Scotland.
What is an allotment?
Extra land people rent to grow fruit and vegetables
A garden centre
A public park
A flower show
Many people in the UK also have gardens at home.
Which garden is in Wales?
Mount Stewart is in Northern Ireland; Kew and Hidcote are in England.
Crathes Castle and Inveraray Castle are in Scotland.
What is the national flower of Scotland?
The daffodil
The shamrock
England: rose; Wales: daffodil; Northern Ireland: shamrock.
Which country is associated with Welsh cakes?
Made from flour, dried fruits and spices.
What are Yorkshire puddings?
Batter baked in the oven, served with roast beef
A sweet dessert
A type of sausage
A fruit cake
Roast beef is associated with England.
Is the statement below true or false? "At 16 you can drink wine or beer with a meal in a hotel or restaurant, as long as you are with someone over 18."
Including eating areas in pubs.
At 16 you can drink wine or beer with a meal in a hotel or restaurant, as long as you are with someone over 18.
Who decides the hours that a pub or night club is open?
The licensee
The local council
Pubs usually open from {#}.{#} am ({#} noon on Sundays).
The same as for gambling clubs.
Is the statement below true or false? "All dogs in public places must wear a collar showing the name and address of the owner."
Owners must also keep dogs under control and clean up after them.
All dogs in public places must wear a collar showing the name and address of the owner.
Which TWO are traditional pub games?
Pool
Bowls
Darts
Chess
Pub quizzes are also popular.
Pool and Darts
When were films first shown publicly in the UK?
Film screenings quickly became popular.
Charlie Chaplin became famous in silent films for which character?
A tramp
A soldier
A pantomime dame
He made a career in Hollywood.
Which director made The 39 Steps (1935) and later worked in Hollywood?
He remained an important director until his death in {#}.
Brief Encounter and Lawrence of Arabia
Ealing Studios.
Nick Park has won Oscars for animated films featuring whom?
Wallace and Gromit
Mr Bean
Paddington Bear
Peter Rabbit
Four Oscars, three for Wallace and Gromit.
Which TWO are the highest-grossing film franchises, produced in the UK?
Star Wars
Many films are now made in the UK by foreign companies.
Harry Potter and James Bond
Also The Ladykillers and the Carry On films.
Private Eye continues the tradition of satire today.
That Was The Week That Was (1960s) and Spitting Image (1980s–90s) were satire.
Which TWO are popular British soap operas?
Coronation Street
Monty Python
EastEnders
Regular soap operas are among the most popular programmes.
Coronation Street and EastEnders
Who can apply for a free TV licence?
People over {#}
Students
Everyone on benefits
Blind people can get a {#}% discount.
Is the statement below true or false? "People who rent different rooms in a shared house with separate tenancy agreements must each buy a TV licence."
Otherwise, one licence covers one home.
People who rent different rooms in a shared house with separate tenancy agreements must each buy a TV licence.
How is the BBC funded?
By TV licences
By advertising
By subscriptions
By the National Lottery
It is the only wholly state-funded media organisation independent of government.
How many national parks are there in England, Wales and Scotland?
Areas of protected countryside everyone can visit.
Why was the clock tower at Parliament named Elizabeth Tower?
For Queen Elizabeth II’s Diamond Jubilee in {#}
After Elizabeth I
For the {#} Olympics
For the Queen’s coronation
The clock is over {#} years old.
Where is the Eden Project?
Devon
Its biomes house plants from all over the world.
Where is the Giant’s Causeway?
The north-east coast of Northern Ireland
The west coast of Scotland
Volcanic lava columns formed about {#} million years ago.
What is the largest expanse of fresh water in mainland Britain?
Windermere
Loch Ness
Lough Neagh
In the Loch Lomond and the Trossachs National Park.
How tall is the London Eye?
{#} feet ({#} metres)
{#},{#} feet ({#} metres)
Built for the millennium.
What is the highest mountain in Wales?
Ben Nevis
Scafell Pike
Pen y Fan
In Snowdonia national park, North Wales.
Who give tours of the Tower of London?
Yeoman Warders (Beefeaters)
Police officers
The Royal Guard
National Trust volunteers
Visitors can also see the Crown Jewels.
What is England’s largest national park?
The Peak District
Dartmoor
Its biggest stretch of water is Windermere.
Secret ballots and Payment for MPs
When was the voting age reduced to {#}?
Why is the British constitution described as "unwritten"?
It is not written down in any single document
It has never been recorded at all
It only exists in spoken tradition
It was lost in the Great Fire
Mainly because the UK has never had a revolution leading to a totally new system.
Which TWO are constitutional institutions in the UK?
The BBC
The judiciary
Also the monarchy, Parliament, the PM, the cabinet, the police and local government.
The civil service and The judiciary
At the start of the {#}th century, who could vote?
Men over {#} who owned a certain amount of property
All men over {#}
All adults
Men and women who owned property
Only a small group of people.
The Chartists’ campaign was seen as a failure at the time, but by 1918 most of their reforms had been adopted.
What type of monarchy does the UK have?
A constitutional monarchy
An absolute monarchy
An elected monarchy
A republic
The monarch does not rule but appoints the government chosen in elections.
Who is the heir apparent to the throne?
Prince Harry
Followed by Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis.
When did Queen Elizabeth II celebrate her Diamond Jubilee?
{#} years as queen. She died on {#} September {#}.
Which TWO are roles of the monarch?
Opening the new parliamentary session each year
Deciding government policy
Receiving foreign ambassadors
Choosing MPs
Policy decisions are made by the PM and cabinet.
Opening the new parliamentary session each year and Receiving foreign ambassadors
The monarch can do which of these in meetings with the Prime Minister?
Advise, warn and encourage
Veto any law
Dismiss ministers at will
Set the budget
Decisions on policy are made by the Prime Minister and cabinet.
All Acts of Parliament are made in the monarch’s name.
What is the difference between the oath and the affirmation of allegiance?
The oath swears by Almighty God; the affirmation does not mention God
The oath is for adults; the affirmation for children
The affirmation is to Parliament; the oath to the King
There is no difference
Both promise to bear true allegiance to King Charles III, his heirs and successors.
Why is the House of Commons regarded as the more important chamber?
Its members are democratically elected
It is older
It is bigger
The King sits there
The PM and almost all of the cabinet are MPs.
Which TWO are responsibilities of MPs?
Representing everyone in their constituency
Appointing judges
Scrutinising what the government is doing
Running the police
MPs also help create laws and debate national issues.
Representing everyone in their constituency and Scrutinising what the government is doing
Since when has the Prime Minister been able to nominate life peers?
Life peers sit only for their own lifetime.
They elect a few of their number to represent them.
Is the statement below true or false? "The House of Commons has powers to overrule the House of Lords, but these are not used often."
The Lords is normally more independent of the government.
The House of Commons has powers to overrule the House of Lords, but these are not used often.
How is the Speaker of the House of Commons chosen?
By other MPs in a secret ballot
By the Prime Minister
By the King
By a public vote
The Speaker is neutral.
The Speaker represents a political party.
How often must a General Election be held?
At least every five years
Every four years
Every three years
MPs are elected at a General Election.
A local council election
An election for the Speaker
An election held every two years
The candidate with the most votes in each constituency wins.
What system was used to elect members of the European Parliament (MEPs)?
Appointment by the PM
A vote by MPs
Seats were allocated in proportion to the total votes each party won.
